evidence: Cic. Sen. 46: ad multam noctem … variō sermōne prōdūcimus
Cic. Phil. 2.24: nē quīnquennī imperium Caesarī prōrogārētur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 13.14.1: auctiōnis diem laxius prōferre (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: drag out (a war, a business); in the passive, drag on
evidence: Cic. Att. 10.8.2: sīn trahitur bellum (Lewis & Short s.v. trahō)

phrases.latin: convīviumque vīcīnōrum cotīdiē compleō, quod ad multam noctem quam maximē possumus variō sermōne prōdūcimus
phrases.english: every day I fill my table with neighbours, and we stretch the party as late into the night as we can with all kinds of talk
